bottleneck:
Long-form watch time has stalled at about 8 h a day because the new Lane A videos aren't getting picked up, and nothing moves viewers from Shorts to long-forms.

(1) **Broken long-forms are the biggest cost, and we're causing it.** The last 4 shipped long-forms (Hair Loss 11-02, Stopping 11-04, Birth Control 11-05, Fatigue 11-06) went out with scenes out of sync with the narration. Content from minute 4–5 shows up 25–65 s in.
- Hair Loss: 6 views, 0 min, 0% average view, 1.64% CTR.
- Fatigue scored 3.5 on visuals with 102 weak shots, and its description was an internal change note.
- Across the 7 Lane A videos since 10-27, the median is 41 min each (Plateau 72, Bones 132, Protein 137, Food Noise 41, Thanksgiving 17, Constipation 10, Hair 0). The 10-16 to 10-24 cohort sits at 564–634 min. Some of that gap is age (3–9 days at the snapshot), but this cohort is below Exp A's 60-min day-7 bar.
- Low retention on those videos (Constipation 23%, Thanksgiving 28%, Protein 31%) keeps YouTube from recommending them, and suggested videos bring 68–84% of Lane A minutes.

(2) **Missed days.** 11-03 and 11-07 had no content at all: 2 of 7 long-form slots lost.

(3) **The funnel is broken by design.** YouTube made links in Shorts descriptions and comments unclickable on 31 Aug 2023. Our "link in the description" Shorts can't send traffic, which is why SHORTS traffic is 0 on all 23 long-forms with traffic data. The 1,019-view hair Short sent nobody anywhere. The only clickable path is the Studio-only related-video link, and it isn't set. End screens aren't set either; PLAYLIST has brought 7 views in total, at 8–12 min each.

(4) **Packaging is getting worse at scale (anecdote; swap timing unconfirmed).**
- Strength: CTR on its new impressions was about 0.6% (+3 clicks on +467 impressions between 11-02 and 11-05).
- What to Eat: about 1.9% on its +568 new impressions.
- Part of that is normal: CTR falls as YouTube shows a video on more surfaces.

(5) **Subscribers.** +2 in 7 days, and 0 since Exp F started. Shorts views also fell to about 130 a day from about 300.

(6) **Blind spot.** The analytics snapshot is stuck at 11-05, so none of the 11-04 to 11-06 long-forms can be judged yet.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook: week of 2026-11-10

**Status: off track.** 147 of 4,000 watch hours, at about 8 h a day; February needs about 35. Subscribers: 383, with +2 in 7 days. Lane A is still the engine, but the last 4 long-forms shipped with scenes out of sync and earn almost nothing. **This week, one clean video beats two broken ones.**

## Long-form (14:00 ET, 8–12 min, `lane: A`)
1. **Repairs come first.** If the owner or QA finds offset beats in Hair Loss (11-02), Stopping (11-04), Birth Control (11-05) or Fatigue (11-06):
   - Re-render from the existing verified script and beat list. No script changes, so no new fact-check is needed beyond the usual audio and frame gates.
   - The publisher uploads the fixed version and sets the broken one to private.
   - A repair counts as that day's long-form. Order: Hair, then Fatigue, Stopping, Birth Control.
2. **New Lane A topics, in this order.** Each answers a question no live video answers. Use label rates with both arms, and keep the prescriber line.
   - "Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: Normal?" (its Short reached 226 views by day 3)
   - "Tirzepatide Dehydration: Signs to Watch For" (use the label's kidney warning)
   - "Tirzepatide Diarrhea: Why It Happens"
   - "Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know". Say what the evidence and label say. Never give a "safe amount". Include the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas.
   - "Tirzepatide Burping and Heartburn: What Helps"
3. Vary the title structure. At most 2 titles a week share an ending. Drug name first, 50 characters or fewer.
4. Still banned in long-form:
   - cost, Medicare, pharmacy and gray-market topics
   - "What is X?" explainers
   - single-trial deep dives
   - news. The only exception is a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide, made public in the last 48 h, as an extra L2.

## Ship-blockers (no deadline overrides these)
- **Beat sync:** export the shot → beat → start-time list from the final narration timings and diff it against the script. After render, check 1 frame per beat for the first 2 minutes. If any headline sits more than 30 s from its beat, rebuild it; don't ship it.
- **Masking 0.02 or lower, measured last, in every slot.** 0.037 shipped on 11-06; that must not happen again.
- **Transcript vs script:** check every number, "point", unit and drug name. Regenerate any scene that fails.
- **Description:** line 1 is empty, followed by the quick answer, the safety block, sources and chapters. Never an internal note. **Publisher: rewrite the L1 11-06 description today.**
- Disclaimer frame, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line go in every piece. The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Packaging
- **Thumbnail:** a change of state (worried → answered), 4 words or fewer, one labelled character, never a body or weight before/after, never repeating the title.
- **Exp E, second video:** the thumbnail designer makes a state-change thumbnail for Strength. The publisher swaps it on 11-10 and logs the time. Change nothing else on Strength or What to Eat until 11-24.

## Retention and linking (long-form)
- The first sentence answers the title, then a "you" scenario. Re-hook every 45–75 s. One subscribe ask, after the payoff.
- End with: "There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description." Never speak a title or say "on screen".
- **Publisher:** line 1 of every long-form description is a ▶ Watch next link (these are clickable on long-forms). Targets:
  - Side Effects → Injection Site
  - What to Eat → Thanksgiving
  - Strength → Bones & Muscle
  - each new video → the closest big-three video
- **Publisher:** every Lane A video goes in the "Life on Tirzepatide" playlist.

## Shorts (3 a day, 170 words or fewer, 60–85 s)
- Shorts description links aren't clickable. The only working path is the owner's related-video link (Exp G). Keep the closing line unchanged until Exp F ends on 11-17.
- **08:00, body-worry reassurance:** "Is this normal?" or "Will it…?", tirzepatide in the title, one new fact, and when to see a doctor.
  - One hair Short is allowed this week, but only once the Hair long-form is verified clean. It needs a new angle that isn't growth or prevalence.
- **13:00, lead:** a tirzepatide-first head-to-head in an obesity population, new retatrutide Phase 3 data or a "what's confirmed?" fact, or a fresh randomized result. At most 1 gray-market Short a week.
- **20:00, funnel:** a fresh question answered by Thanksgiving (on 2 days ahead of the Nov 18–27 peak), Side Effects, What to Eat or Bones & Muscle. Log the target in the post notes so the owner can set the related-video link.
- **Exp F:** on 08:00 and 13:00 only, the second-to-last line is "We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps." Then "Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description." It was missing twice on 11-06, which contaminates the test. Count both lines in the 170 words.
- **Banned:**
  - "Approved yet?" titles and "3 Ways" lists
  - brand-first titles, and semaglutide-only titles unless the evidence is semaglutide-only
  - cost, surgery, observational and grocery angles
  - titles that name no drug, and drug names nobody searches for
- Any one trial in at most 1 Short a week, and a new fact in every piece.

## Carousels
- Make one only if the scheduler asks for it, and reuse verified Short text only.

## Analyst
- Get the snapshot past 11-05 before any read. Log the 11-04 to 11-06 long-forms at day 7.
- Log daily minutes for Strength and What to Eat, plus each Short's subscribersGained at day 7 (Exp F).
- Log SHORTS traffic on every long-form targeted by a related-video link (Exp G).

## Hold constant
- 14:00 ET long slot, 8–12 min, the retention rules, the long-form subscribe ask, and the Shorts closing line.

experiments.name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
experiments.hypothesis: Long-tail practical tirzepatide questions that people search for beat approved-drug deep dives and keep gaining views over time.
experiments.change: Lane A on every day without qualifying news, with the long-tail searched question first in the title.
experiments.metric: Success: day-7 median of 25+ views and 60+ watch minutes, still growing at day 28.
experiments.result: Won at n=8+. It earns 71% of tracked long-form minutes, and the big three have 564–634 min each. Caveat from this week: the 7 Lane A videos since 10-27 have a median of only about 41 min (0–137) at 3–9 days old. The last 4 shipped with scenes out of sync, so this looks like a production failure, not proof the lane is weakening. Lane A stays the default, with the beat-sync check as a ship-blocker.

experiments.name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
experiments.hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane would also work as long-form.
experiments.change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B.
experiments.result: Closed early at n=1. The pharmacy check got 19 views and 61 min. Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

experiments.name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
experiments.hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public named trial result drives more long-form views than evergreen topics.
experiments.change: The long-form slot went to qualifying fresh randomized results.
experiments.result: Retired at n=1 (petrelintide: 37 views, 160 min). Looking back at fresh next-gen results, the median is about 35 views. News goes to 13:00 Shorts. Only a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide may get an extra L2.

experiments.name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified description link
experiments.hypothesis: A 20:00 Short that asks a fresh question a live long-form answers, with a verified description link, lifts that long-form's daily views.
experiments.change: The 20:00 Short pointed to a live Lane A long-form, with 'link in the description'.
experiments.metric: The target long-form's views in the 3 days after the Short vs the 3 days before, plus its SHORTS traffic.
experiments.min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link
experiments.result: Closed with no valid data point. The way it was meant to work can't work: YouTube made links in Shorts descriptions and comments unclickable on 31 Aug 2023. That explains why SHORTS traffic is 0 on all 23 long-forms with traffic data. Replaced by Exp G, which uses the Studio related-video link, the only clickable link in the Shorts player.

experiments.name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail (What to Eat, plus Strength as a second test)
experiments.hypothesis: Our two most-shown practical videos have a packaging problem, not a discovery problem. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer lifts CTR toward the 3.8–4.7% that Side Effects, How Long and Protein get.
experiments.change: Only the thumbnail changes, no body imagery. What to Eat was swapped on about 11-04 (publisher must confirm the time). Strength is swapped on 11-10 as a second test of the same change. No other edits to either video for 14 days.
experiments.metric: CTR on impressions after the swap vs CTR just before it, judged per video and with views per day not falling. Before-swap baselines: What to Eat about 1.9% on 568 impressions (11-02→11-05), 2.53% overall; Strength about 0.6% on 467 impressions, 2.10% overall. Success: new-impression CTR of 3.0%+ on both.
experiments.min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days per video, whichever comes later (What to Eat around 11-18, Strength around 11-24)
experiments.result: Not readable yet, and the analytics feed is stuck at 11-05. Watch-out: CTR naturally falls as impressions spread to more surfaces, so compare against the before-swap rate, not the overall average.

experiments.name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double Shorts subscriber conversion (about 0.5–0.6 per 1,000 views).
experiments.change: On 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts only, the second-to-last line is 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' 20:00 Shorts get no line and act as the control.
experiments.metric: subscribersGained per 1,000 views at day 7, line vs control. Also channel subscribers per day vs the 1.3-a-day baseline. Success: 2× the control rate and 2.5+ channel subscribers a day.
experiments.min_sample: 14 days (11-03 to 11-17), about 28 Shorts with the line and 14 without
experiments.result: Early channel-level read is weak: +0 subscribers since 11-04 (5 days) vs a 1.3-a-day baseline. That's confounded by Shorts views falling to about 130 a day (from about 300), two missed days, and the line missing on 2 Shorts on 11-06. Per-Short day-7 data starts 11-11. If the channel is still under 1 subscriber a day at day 14, close it as lost.

experiments.name: Exp G: Studio related-video link on top Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: The related-video link is the only clickable path from a Short. Setting it on our highest-view body-worry Shorts will create SHORTS traffic to Lane A long-forms. Those viewers watch at long-form rates and subscribe about 5× more often than Shorts viewers.
experiments.change:
The owner sets one related-video link on each of these Shorts:
- hair grow-back (1,019 views) → the Hair long-form once it's verified clean, Side Effects until then
- bones (242) → Bones & Muscle
- injection site (226) → Side Effects
- nausea (166) → Side Effects
- muscle (136) → Strength
- breakfast (111) → What to Eat
- constipation fibre (92) → Constipation
- Thanksgiving Short (11-06) → Thanksgiving
No other change to those Shorts.
experiments.metric: SHORTS-source views and minutes on each target long-form in the 7 days after the link vs 0 before. Success: at least 1 long-form view per 100 new Short views across the set, plus a visible rise in channel subscribers.
experiments.min_sample: 8 linked Shorts, 7 days after the link is set
experiments.result: Waiting on the owner. It starts the day the links are set. It needs advanced features turned on in Studio.

owner_decisions: Check the last 4 long-forms and re-upload the broken ones (today, about 15 min). Watch the first 2 minutes of Hair Loss (11-02), Stopping (11-04), Birth Control (11-05) and Fatigue (11-06). If scenes are out of sync, have the pipeline re-render and re-upload each one, then set the broken copy to private. Why: QA flagged all 4. Hair Loss has 6 views and 0 minutes, and the 7 Lane A videos since 10-27 earn a median of about 41 min vs 564–634 for the big three. Out-of-sync videos lose viewers early, so YouTube stops recommending them, and suggested videos bring 68–84% of our long-form minutes. Expected effect: if the 4 repaired videos earn even Bones-level minutes (about 130 each in the first week), that's roughly +1.2 h a day once they're picked up. They have almost no views, so taking the broken copies private costs nothing.

Set the related-video link on 8 Shorts in Studio (about 10 min; needs advanced features turned on). Targets:
- hair grow-back → Side Effects (Hair Loss once fixed)
- bones → Bones & Muscle
- injection site → Side Effects
- nausea → Side Effects
- muscle → Strength
- breakfast → What to Eat
- constipation fibre → Constipation
- Thanksgiving Short → Thanksgiving
Why: YouTube made links in Shorts descriptions unclickable in Aug 2023, so 'link in the description' can't send anyone. SHORTS traffic is 0 on all 23 long-forms with traffic data, and the 1,019-view hair Short sent nobody. This is Exp G. Expected effect: the first real Shorts → long-form traffic. At 1 click per 100 Short views and about 5 min a view, that's a few hours a week now, growing with every new Short you link, plus subscribers from long-form viewers.

Add end screens to Side Effects, What to Eat and Strength (about 10 min): one best-for-viewer video plus the 'Life on Tirzepatide' playlist. Why: END_SCREEN traffic is 0, and playlist views run 8–12 min vs about 5 for suggested. These 3 videos have 1,622–2,052 impressions each and bring 71% of our long-form minutes. Expected effect: longer sessions and pickup for Bones, Plateau, Constipation and Thanksgiving ahead of the Nov 18–27 Thanksgiving peak.

Find out why 11-03 and 11-07 had no content at all. Why: that's 2 of 7 long-form slots lost in a week where every Lane A video counts. We need about 30 mature Lane A videos to reach about 35 h a day. Expected effect: +2 long-forms and +6 Shorts a week if the pipeline runs every day.

Fix the analytics job (stuck at the 11-05 snapshot) and confirm that What to Eat's new thumbnail went live on 11-04, with the time. Why: the 11-04 to 11-06 long-forms can't be judged, and Exp E has no clean start time. Expected effect: valid reads for Exp E and Exp F on 11-17/18 instead of another lost week.

Remove the Tue/Fri carousels (delete carouselDays and the 17:30 slot in config/channel.json). Why: about 50 carousels reached 0–4 people each, and one was still made on 11-06. Expected effect: the freed Claude usage and production time go to re-renders and the frame-by-frame beat check.
